verses.text: "These are the laws you must set before the people:
If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year he is to go free without paying anything.
If he came alone, he is to leave alone. If he had a wife when he came, she is to go with him.
If his master gives him a wife and she has sons or daughters, the woman and her children belong to her master. Only the man will go free.
But if the servant says clearly, 'I love my master, my wife, and my children. I do not want to go free,'
then his master must take him to God. He must take him to the door or the doorpost and push a sharp tool through his ear. Then he will be his servant for life.
If a man sells his daughter as a servant, she is not to go free the way male servants do.
If she does not please the master who chose her for himself, he must let her be bought back. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, because he has broken his promise to her.
If he chooses her for his son, he must treat her like a daughter.
If he marries another woman, he must not take away from the first one her food, her clothing, or her rights as a wife.
If he does not give her these three things, she may go free without paying any money.
Anyone who hits a person and kills him must be put to death.
But if he did not plan it, and God let it happen, he may run away to a place I will choose for you.
But if someone plans and kills another person on purpose, take him away even from my altar and put him to death.
Anyone who attacks his father or his mother must be put to death.
Anyone who kidnaps another person must be put to death, whether he has sold the person or still has him.
Anyone who curses his father or his mother must be put to death.
Suppose two men are fighting, and one hits the other with a stone or with his fist. The injured man does not die, but he has to stay in bed.

If he later gets up and walks around outside with a walking stick, the man who hit him will not be punished. But he must pay the injured man for the time he lost, and take care of him until he is completely healed.
If a man beats his male or female slave with a stick, and the slave dies on the spot, the man must be punished.
But if the slave gets up after a day or two, the owner is not to be punished, because the slave is his property.
Suppose men are fighting and hurt a pregnant woman, and she gives birth too early, but there is no serious injury. The man who hurt her must pay whatever her husband asks and the judges allow.
But if there is serious injury, you must take life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
If a man hits his male or female servant in the eye and destroys it, he must let the servant go free to pay for the eye.
If he knocks out a tooth of his male or female servant, he must let the servant go free to pay for the tooth.
If a bull kills a man or a woman with its horns, the bull must be stoned to death, and its meat must not be eaten. But the owner of the bull will not be held responsible.

But suppose the bull has had the habit of attacking people, and the owner has been warned but has not kept it penned up. If it then kills a man or a woman, the bull must be stoned, and its owner must also be put to death.
But if the owner is allowed to pay money instead, he must pay whatever is demanded to save his life.
The same law applies if the bull attacks a son or a daughter.
If the bull attacks a male or female slave, the owner must pay the slave's master thirty pieces of silver, and the bull must be stoned.
Suppose a man uncovers a pit, or digs one and does not cover it, and a bull or a donkey falls into it.
The owner of the pit must pay for the loss. He must pay its owner, and the dead animal will belong to him.
If one man's bull hurts another man's bull and it dies, they must sell the live bull and share the money. They must also share the dead animal.
But if everyone knew that the bull had the habit of attacking, and its owner did not keep it penned up, the owner must pay, a live bull for the dead one, and the dead animal will be his.
